section.title: CSS vs Tailwind CSS — Styling Approaches
section.subtitle: Hand-written stylesheets vs utility-first classes — how each approach styles modern UIs.

css.definition: CSS is a declarative styling language — you write rules in .css files that target elements by selector, then apply classes or ids in HTML.

tailwind.definition: Tailwind is utility-first — instead of writing CSS, you compose styles from hundreds of small utility classes directly in your HTML/JSX.
tailwind.code:
Hello
/* Compiles to minimal CSS — only classes you use -->

css.definition: You write a flex container rule in CSS and control direction, gap and alignment with properties like display:flex, justify-content and gap.

tailwind.definition: The same flexbox properties exist as utilities — flex, flex-row, justify-between, items-center, gap-4 — applied straight in markup.
tailwind.code:
Left
Right
/* gap-4 = 1rem, justify-between, items-center */

css.definition: You define arbitrary values in CSS: padding: 16px, margin-top: 8px, color: #3b82f6, background: linear-gradient(...). Custom properties (--vars) help reuse values.

tailwind.definition: Spacing uses a 4px scale (p-4 = 1rem), colors are named shades (bg-blue-500), and sizes map to the same scale — no custom values needed for 95% of cases.
tailwind.code:
<button class="px-5 py-2.5 mt-3 bg-blue-500
  text-white rounded-lg hover:bg-blue-600">
  Click
</button>

/* px-5 = 1.25rem, py-2.5, mt-3, rounded-lg */

css.definition: Media queries in CSS flip styles at breakpoints — you write separate rules inside @media blocks for mobile/tablet/desktop.

tailwind.definition: Breakpoints are prefixes on utilities — sm:, md:, lg:, xl: — so responsiveness lives inline in the same class attribute.

css.definition: Full freedom — any value, any selector, any pseudo-class. Custom properties (CSS variables) enable theming; preprocessors like Sass add loops and mixins.

tailwind.definition: Extend via tailwind.config.js — add custom colors, spacing, fonts, breakpoints. The JIT compiler only emits CSS for classes you actually use.

topics.title: When to Use Which
topics.learn: Choosing the right tool for the job.

css.definition: Plain CSS wins for unique one-off designs, tiny sites, email templates, and when you need pixel-perfect control or exotic effects (animations, blend modes, clip-path).

tailwind.definition: Tailwind wins for rapid UI development, consistent design systems, React/Vue/Next projects, and teams that want styling colocation without naming-paralysis.
